title: P0 — Windows-native runtime: kernel-HANDLE artifact security + native Codex executor
description: P0 Windows-native runtime + R1 audit corrections. WS-A: win32-object-io.ts binds governed fs steps to kernel HANDLEs (NtCreateFile RootDirectory-relative = /proc/self/fd parity, opened-object path/identity, atomic no-replace publish, dir FlushFileBuffers, OPEN_REPARSE_POINT = O_NOFOLLOW). WS-B: native win32 codex resolution (.exe preferred over .cmd), windows.sandbox='elevated' verified on real codex (CodexSandboxOffline), async error→FAILED, timeout/cancel intact. WS-C: real-seam ingest gate; delegated mission COMPLETES on Windows. R1-F1: pnpm-lock.yaml carries koffi; frozen-lockfile install clean. R1-F2: materializeEntryWin32 temp HANDLE single-ownership closeTmp; collision branch deletes+closes temp BEFORE opening raced dest (no handle reuse); C9/C10 collision regressions (converge identical, fail closed divergent, dest survives). R1-F3: openObject file opens default GENERIC_READ|SYNCHRONIZE; dirs keep RW for fsync; A13 write-deny DACL file ingests, A14 readonly-attr file ingests, A15 deny-read control stays closed. R1-F4: WIN32_CMD_ARG_SAFE strips cmd metacharacters (&|<>'"%^!()[];#$?* backtick newline); batch tokens per-token quoted under /d /s /c with /s-safe outer pair; spawn uses windowsVerbatimArguments; batch-lookalike/metachar paths (codex.cmd&calc) fail closed; native .exe bypasses COMSPEC. R2-F5: closeTmp reports whether delete-on-close was armed and always releases the HANDLE; the collision branch fails closed (tmp_cleanup) when cleanup is unverifiable — never MATERIALIZED on unverified cleanup; the unwind path keeps the original error dominant; the raced destination is never mutated by temp cleanup; C11/C12 fault-injection regressions (deleteOnClose=false → fail closed, dest unchanged, temp handle closed exactly once).
